title: 停车没位也能谈：交警说好吧，梵蒂冈留下的习惯？
speaker: Jason Horowitz

segments.en: Talk about the importance of Vatican plays in life in Rome today.
segments.zh: 谈谈梵蒂冈在当今罗马生活中的重要性。

segments.en: And the great which you, a guy from Fresh Meadows, Queens, really had to bone up on a lot of the stuff, you know, before.
segments.zh: 而你，一个来自皇后区新鲜草原的人，之前真的得恶补很多这些东西。

segments.en: Yeah, yeah, I mean, so the Catholic Church sort of imbues everything in Italy, right? I mean, it ran the place.
segments.zh: 是的，天主教会渗透在意大利的一切中，对吧？它曾统治这里。

segments.en: The papal states, the middle of the country was under the Pope. He was the king, and you still see it in many, many different ways.
segments.zh: 教皇国，中部地区曾归教皇管辖。他就是国王，你仍能在很多方面看到这一点。

segments.en: One way that I sort of ran into it is authority. So everything is sort of negotiable, right?
segments.zh: 我遇到的一个方面是权威。所以一切都可以协商，对吧？

segments.en: I love my people, so there's positives and negatives to this, right?
segments.zh: 我爱我的人民，所以这有好有坏，对吧？

segments.en: But like, you know, even your traffic cop, right? If you park parking very badly, and my wife is an infamously bad parker.
segments.zh: 但比如，就连交通警察也是。如果你停车停得很糟，我妻子是出了名的停车差。

segments.en: And I would say to her, a wonderful parker but in a bad place, and I would say to her, you know, this is not a spot.
segments.zh: 我会对她说，停得真好但地方不对，我会说，这不是停车位。

segments.en: And there's like a vigile, there's a traffic cop coming over, and she say he understands. And in fact there was like a negotiation, like there's nowhere else to go, and he'd say okay.
segments.zh: 有个交警走过来，她说他理解。事实上就像谈判，说没别的地方可去，他就说好吧。

segments.en: And that's very, very Catholic in a way, right? It's very human. It's like everything, you know, in a negative way you end up with bribery.
segments.zh: 这在某种程度上非常天主教，对吧？非常人性。就像一切，负面的话最终会变成贿赂。

segments.en: And you know, usually you know, but in the positive way you can sort of, you know, if there are extenuating circumstances, they matter, right?
segments.zh: 通常你知道，但正面的话，如果有情有可原的情况，它们很重要，对吧？

segments.en: And so that's one way that I constantly came into contact with it.
segments.zh: 这是我一直接触到它的一种方式。

segments.en: But on the flip side, Italians are also extremely anti-authoritarian.
segments.zh: 但另一方面，意大利人也极其反权威。

segments.en: And I think that also comes from the Vatican. I think that they didn't like having the Vatican telling them what to do for a long time.
segments.zh: 我认为这也来自梵蒂冈。他们长期不喜欢梵蒂冈指手画脚。

segments.en: And so Italy as a country is born in response to the Vatican. It doesn't want the Vatican.
segments.zh: 所以意大利作为一个国家是回应梵蒂冈而诞生的。它不想要梵蒂冈。

segments.en: Yeah, so everything. Talk to him about what it's like to cover a conclave.
segments.zh: 是的，所以一切。跟他谈谈报道教皇选举会议是什么感觉。
